statement: Perturbed MC MST restarts (random noise on metric closure weights + Kruskal rebuild) improve score by ~0.08 points over the unperturbed MC MST baseline. The time-limited loop explores alternative MST topologies that lead to different relay assignments. The improvement is modest because the original MST is already near-optimal for most test cases.
regime: Problem #211 with N=K=1500. Perturbation epsilon range [0.002, 0.102]. LCG seed 54321. Time budget 9 seconds within 10-second test limit.
mechanism: Adding random noise to MC weights before building Kruskal's MST explores alternative near-optimal tree topologies. Different topologies lead to different relay selections after subgraph MST + prune + greedy insert, some of which yield lower actual cost. The improvement is consistent but small (+0.082 points) because the unperturbed MST topology is already good for most test cases (6/10 tests at or near perfect score).
applicability_bounds: Requires sufficient time budget for multiple perturbation trials. Under CPU contention, the time-limited loop may produce too few trials, reducing or eliminating the improvement. The improvement diminishes as the base algorithm approaches optimal.

statement: Relay reassignment + degree-3 hub insertion provides ~0.13 points of improvement beyond what perturbed restarts alone achieve. These post-processing steps capture opportunities that greedy degree-2 insertion misses: suboptimal relay positions (reassignment) and 3-robot hub connections (degree-3 insertion).
regime: Problem #211 with N=K=1500. Reassignment rounds: 20. Hub search top-K: 8, rounds: 5.
mechanism: After greedy insertion places relays one-at-a-time (degree-2 splits), two independent post-processing steps capture remaining opportunities: (1) relay reassignment checks if moving a used relay to an unused position better serves its neighbors — this matters when greedy's sequential decisions left a relay in a position that is locally but not globally optimal; (2) degree-3 hub insertion finds unused relays that can connect 3 robots through a single hub, removing 2 tree edges and adding 3 hub edges — this captures savings that degree-2 insertion structurally cannot.
applicability_bounds: The improvement is from two distinct mechanisms. Hub insertion requires the Steiner subtree savings formula (pm_max + pm_min - hub_cost) to correctly identify valid 3-robot connections. Reassignment requires iterating over all unused relays for each used relay.

statement: The three enhancement mechanisms (perturbed restarts, relay reassignment, degree-3 hub insertion) are additive: their combined improvement (+0.211) equals the sum of individual contributions (~0.082 from restarts + ~0.129 from post-processing = ~0.211). There are no significant interaction effects between the mechanisms.
regime: Problem #211 with N=K=1500. Full combined algorithm vs restarts-only ablation.
mechanism: The three mechanisms operate on independent dimensions of the solution space: restarts change the MST topology (which edges are in the tree), reassignment changes which relay serves each edge (relay identity), and hub insertion changes the connectivity pattern (degree-2 vs degree-3). Because they modify orthogonal aspects of the solution, their improvements don't interfere and stack additively.
applicability_bounds: Additivity holds when the mechanisms target different suboptimalities. If the solution becomes near-perfect (all tests scoring 10.0), the mechanisms would compete for the same diminishing margin and additivity would break.
